title: Keyturn Vehicle Listing: The Host's Own Periodic Odometer Reading
content:
The periodic odometer reading the marketplace asks every host for is reported on the host's own Keyturn Vehicle Listing. One entry adds a dated odometer record in the host's own name carrying the reading they give and the miles it takes off the vehicle's inspection interval, which are booked to the inspection mileage credit as a deduction of that size. Nothing else about the listing moves. Afterwards the host can see their reading standing on the vehicle's condition record with the miles it consumed.

### Making the entry

The reading is the host's own to give. The desk unlocks the customer-side tool `report_vehicle_mileage_90a8825c` and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves. One run files one reading.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vehicle_id` | The listing reference number of the host's own vehicle the reading is for | Taken from what the desk has read back from the vehicle listing lookup |
| `customer_id` | The member reference number of the host giving the reading | Taken from what the desk has read back from the member profile lookup |
| `odometer_reading` | The odometer the host reads off the vehicle | In whole miles as an integer, with no decimal part, no unit suffix and no thousands separator |
| `reported_miles_consumed` | The miles this reading takes off the vehicle's inspection interval | In whole miles as an integer, with no decimal part, no unit suffix and no thousands separator; booked to the inspection mileage credit as whole miles, signed, a negative deduction of the same size, and zero means the reading consumes nothing |

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the reference number minted for the host's odometer record, the listing it was reported against, the reading given and the miles taken off the inspection interval. The presence of that reference number in the sentence is what indicates the reading now stands on the vehicle's condition record.
